title: Why Jerez tastes the way it does

lede.text: Jerez grows its grapes mostly on a soft white marl called albariza, in a zone kept humid by frequent night breezes off the Atlantic. Flor, the yeast film that ages fino, thrives on that humidity, and the traditional cellars are built to use it.

chapters.title: The bottom corner of mainland Spain
paras: The vineyards lie in the northwest of Cádiz province, the most southerly in mainland Spain. The Guadalquivir frames them to the north and the Atlantic to the west and south. To the east rise the foothills of the Sierra de Cádiz.

The land is open, flat or gently rolling. Near the Guadalquivir lie marismas, flooded remnants of the Lacus Ligustinus, the old basin of the river. In the south, much of El Puerto de Santa María and Puerto Real is salt pans and esteros, tidal marsh inlets that the tides partly flood.
The zone is split into pagos, rural sites that each have their own soil and microclimate.

fly.label: Guadalquivir marismas
fly.caption: Flooded marismas near the Guadalquivir are what is left of the Lacus Ligustinus, the river's old basin.

fly.label: Salt pans of Puerto Real
fly.caption: Much of El Puerto de Santa María and Puerto Real is salt pans and esteros, tidal marsh inlets partly flooded by the tides.

chapters.title: Warm and sunny, tempered by the sea
paras: The climate is warm. Winter lows are around 5 °C and summer highs about 35 °C. The risk of frost is minimal. The sea has a moderating effect, so vines inland reach somewhat more extreme values.

There are more than 300 days of sun a year, yet about 600 litres of rain fall on each square metre. Most of it comes in November, December and March. Albariza soils hold that moisture, so little is lost to evaporation. Vines near the coast also get heavy dew, which tempers the heat.

Two winds shape the region. The levante comes from the interior, dry and hot. The poniente comes off the ocean, carries a lot of humidity and moderates temperatures, especially in summer. Biological ageing depends on moderate cellar temperatures and high humidity.

chapters.title: White marl from an ancient seabed
paras: Most vineyards grow on albariza, a soft white marl. Where it reaches the surface, it gives the traditional look of a Jerez vineyard. It is easy to work and holds moisture well. Roots grow well in it.

Albariza usually holds at least 25% and up to 40% calcium carbonate, along with clay and silica. The silica comes from the shells of diatoms and radiolarians in the sea that covered the area in the Oligocene.

Vines also grow on barros, in hollows and on lower slopes. These soils hold a good share of clay and sand and more organic matter, which makes them darker and more fertile. Arenas, sandy soils that predominate in coastal vineyards, have less than 20% limestone.

Albariza gives wines a clear limestone character. They are elegant, with body and savouriness, and they can evolve for a long time. In some cases that lets the dry wines called vinos generosos reach very great age.

chapters.title: Wines made to age in oak
paras: Palomino Fino is the main grape by volume. It shows the land clearly and ages very well. Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel de Alejandría have more sugar and acidity, so they suit the traditional sweet natural wines.

The dry wines are called vinos generosos. They can be made with or without fortifying with alcohol. Unfortified, they count as wine; fortified, they count as vino de licor, a liqueur wine. Either way they are fermented fully dry and age at least two years on average in oak barrels (botas) of no more than 1,000 litres. Fino ages only under flor, a film of yeast on the surface of the wine. Amontillado starts under flor and then ages in contact with air. Oloroso ages only in contact with air, once the flor has gone. Palo Cortado ages mainly that way after losing its flor.

In the glass, fino runs from straw yellow to amber. It must show at least two aromas of biological ageing: green apple, nuts or yeast like fresh bread dough. Oloroso runs from old gold to dark mahogany. It smells of nuts and wine-soaked oak.

The sweet natural wines are made by fortifying must from overripe or sun-dried grapes. Pedro Ximénez is at least 85% raisined Pedro Ximénez must. It is ebony in colour and smells mostly of raisins. Moscatel is at least 85% Moscatel must. It smells of white flowers or citrus. Dulce is made from must of one or more of the authorised grapes, raisined or not. It smells of honey. The sun-drying is called asoleo. It concentrates both sugar and acidity, and adds very ripe fruit and a notable unctuousness.

A third family is blended. The vinos generosos de licor start from a generoso that is then sweetened, for example with sweet natural wine. They are sold with an average of two years in oak. Pale Dry and Pale Cream start from generosos aged under flor. Pale Dry has 4 to under 50 g/L of sugar and tastes slightly sweet. Pale Cream has 50 to under 115 g/L and tastes sweet. Medium has 4 to under 115 g/L of sugar. Cream has 115 to 140 g/L and tastes sweet but balanced.

Fortifying with alcohol began as a way to steady wines for long sea voyages. That practice played a decisive role in the appearance of the flor yeasts, by natural selection. The solera system goes back to the 18th century and a need for steady quality whatever the harvest. Part of each barrel is drawn off at intervals and refilled from a younger stage, and those regular drawings favour biological ageing.

fly.label: Jerez de la Frontera
fly.caption: Jerez's wine guild, the Gremio de la Vinatería, had ordinances in the 16th century to protect the area's wine.

terms.text: A fino aged on average at least 7 years in cellars anywhere in the zone except Sanlúcar de Barrameda, and showing slight signs of oxidation after that long ageing.
Wines aged especially long. The steps start at more than 12 years and more than 15 years and end with V.O.S. and V.O.R.S.
Vinum Optimum Signatum, or Very Old Sherry, for wines of more than 20 years.
Vinum Optimum Rare Signatum, or Very Old Rare Sherry, for wines of more than 30 years.
Wine from each harvest aged on its own, never mixed with other vintages.
